[title25][sentence]
You assume that this ornate parlor
must have belonged to someone wealthy
and powerful.  Beautifully painted
portraits adorn the walls; rare porcelain
pieces sit on small custom shelves; and
in the middle of it all, a unique-looking vase
sits on a majestic pedestal.

and powerful.  Beautifully painted
portraits adorn the walls and rare
porcelain pieces sit on small custom

[title18][sentence]\nBlack and white tiles interlock to\nform the solid marble floor.

[title19][sentence]
Several large pillars reach majestically
toward the ceiling.  They appear to be
solid marble.
[title24][sentence]\nThe small fragile teacups appears to be\nmade of  extremely fine porcelain.
[title25][sentence]\nDainty teacups aren't you style; you're\nmore of a 'dirty coffee mug' kind of guy.

[title25][sentence]
Although pretty, this vase does not
match the description Colonel Stone gave
you.

[title26][sentence]
Three hand-painted oil paintings grace
the northern wall of the room.  There
appears to be a family resemblance
between these gentlemen, but you do not
recognize any of them.  There are
nameplates beneath each portrait.

[title20][sentence]
From left to right they read:
"Sputatious T. Bigfish", "W. Widepipe Bigfish",
and "Benjamin Deeppost Bigfish".  The devious
looks in their eyes convince you that these
portraits represent three generations of
politicians.

[title29][sentence]
Several portraits and porcelain pieces
decorate the walls of this lavish parlor.
You can't help but feel that there is something
odd about the decorative metal studs that
line the tops of the walls.
[title19][sentence]\nA lovely violet crystal vase sits\natop the decorative pedestal.
[title20][sentence]\nThe pedestal appears odd without the\nvase sitting on it.

[title22][sentence]
The bottle doesn't seem appropriate
sitting on the ornate pedestal, but it
did fool the security system.

[title27][sentence]
You have become completely familiar
with the teleporters.  This unit, however,
is the most tastefully decorated teleporter
you have seen.  It is obviously a privately
owned unit.

[title19][sentence]
This is it!  You are elated to finally be
within arms reach of Colonel Stone's
precious vase!  Light scintillates through
the lavender-colored crystal.

[title27][sentence]
Nice security system.  The moment you
lifted that vase off the pedestal, you had
a bad accident involving a half dozen
laser beams.  You have only a few
seconds to ponder the problem before
your scorched body expires.
[title25][sentence]\nThat won't work, the [noun1] is\nmuch too heavy.
[title25][sentence]\nThat won't work, the [noun1] is\nfar too light.

[title21][sentence]
Unfortunately, the bottle was too light.
You consider the gravity of your error
as small wisps of smoke curl up from
the depths of your thoracic cavity.

[title25][sentence]
Unfortunately, the bottle was too heavy.
You have mere moments to consider
your error before the charred remains
of your heart issue a final thump.

[title32][sentence]
At last!  After all you've been through,
you finally have your hands on Colonel
Stone's precious vase!  The many possible
uses for 75,000 galactars flash through your head:
a new ship, Lolita, a lifetime supply of fire wood, Lolita,  . . . .

[title32][sentence]
That would be pretty foolish, considering
the elaborate procedures you just went
through to defeat the security system.

[title32][sentence]
The bottle now rests on the pedestal, and
apparently has just the right amount of
water in it to fool the security system.
You saw that trick in a movie once, and you
are glad you got it right, since you wouldn't
want to be chased through the room by a giant
boulder.

[title27][sentence]
You are at the edge of the city, beneath
the gigantic cylindrical perimeter wall,
in front of a large glass viewport.

[title30][sentence]
As you look out into the ocean you
pause and think.  The engineering that
went in to this city amazes you.  Building
a metropolis in a volcano cone BELOW
sea-level is quite an accomplishment.

[title26][sentence]
As you look out into the ocean you
pause and think.  The engineering that
went into this city amazes you.  Building
a metropolis in a volcano comb BELOW
sea-level is quite an accomplishment.
Something in the water seems to have taken
an interest in you.

[title27][sentence]
You are standing at the base of the
cylindrical perimeter wall.  The
viewport is recessed into the wall,
suggesting that the wall is quite
thick.
[title21][sentence]\nYou don't want to look at another\nair vent for the rest of your life.

[title22][sentence]
The indicator is giving an indication
indicative of something indicating
something else.  Just what that
indication is escapes you completely.

[title22][sentence]
The sculpture resembles a cube with
a lightning bolt glued to it.  You do
not understand the significance of this
shape.

[title20][sentence]
This is the car you arrived in.
It still looks the same as when you
got here.

[title22][sentence]
The small fountain under the statue
is not currently running.  The water
in the pool is probably stagnant.

[title27][sentence]
A thought:  If you want to blow the
viewport up, don't you think you
should be able to get away first?
Setting that bomb off in your hands
would not be good for your
complexion.

[title29][sentence]
You carefully place the time bomb on the
small ledge in front of the window.  You
set the timer for five minutes, but get a little
nervous when the timer jumps from 4:49 to
4:02.  This timer must be a little flaky--you
should probably seek safety NOW!
[title17][sentence]\nDon't you think you should be leaving\nright about now?
[title25][sentence]\nYou carefully disarm the time bomb,\nand slip it back in your pocket.

[title32]NOVICE LEVEL WARNING
Watch out!  Blowing up that window
will commit you irrevocably to a course
of action.  You don't yet have everything
you need to solve the puzzles in the next
section of the game, so blowing it up now
would prevent you from winning.  Go back
and search carefully, then try putting the
bomb on the ledge again later when you think
you are ready.  In particular, be sure to
bring something yummy to feed to that sea
monster.

[title32]INTERMEDIATE LEVEL WARNING
Watch out!  Blowing up that window
will commit you irrevocably to a course
of action.  If you haven't found everything
you need to solve the puzzles in the next
section of the game, blowing up the window
now will prevent you from winning.  We therefore
suggest that you save your game now.  Then,
issue this command again to place the bomb.
That way, if you get stuck, you can come back
to this point and find the additional items
that you need.

[title26][sentence]

maintenance platform.  A pile of bones lies
scattered around the teleporter entrance.

[title27][sentence]
The rim of the city is obviously the top
of the volcano cone.  The short section
you are standing on has been paved, and
you imagine that it must be a maintenance
platform.
[title26][sentence]\nYou have no clues as to what purpose\nthis cement block could possibly have served.

that expressed an interest in your nutritional
value at the viewport in the city.  He seems to
be trying to decide if you are an appetizer or
an entree.  You should probably act with haste.

[title27][sentence]
A few monster chunks still float around
just below the surface.  You can't see
anything of the city you destroyed.

[title25][sentence]

with a large hungry-looking cycloptic
beast.  You may want to do something
instead of just sitting there like an hors d'oeuvre.

have more immediate concerns than
the building.

above the waves.  Every other building

dark water.

monster certainly won't be bothering

note that the bottle now feels extremely
heavy.

The gaudiest bedroom in the known universe
unfolds before your eyes.  You get the feeling
that Bruce must have been an actor.  Various
theatrical memorabilia adorn the walls.  A think
layer of dust covers everything here.

[title32][sentence]
A fluffy feather mattress lies atop a
purple molded plastic frame bed.
You are a little tired, but you know
you have better things to do than
take a nap just now.  Besides, you
would probably asphyxiate in the
dust cloud that would rise were you
to try to lie down here.

[title29][sentence]

each with it's own stand.  They are
small styrofoam figures in the shape
of a humanoid head.
[title20][sentence]\nYou don't have any wigs, and\ntherefore don't need any stands.

[title26][sentence]
A magazine review of Bruce's first stage
performance.  You scan it quickly.  Only
the passages ". . . could swear they were real . . ."
and ". . . thought the enemy had broken in . . ."
stick in your mind.  The reviewer must have
liked the show; he gave it four-and-a-half
stars.

[title32][sentence]
The laminated and framed theater tickets
bear the name of the show: "Love Thy Enemy".
These tickets must have been for one of
Bruce's performances.

[title24][sentence]
You see  a tall woman in front of a theater
on opening night.  You are just about to
comment on her legs when you realize this
must be Bruce.  You swallow hard and
stare at the floor for a moment.

[title27][sentence]
The various lamps about the room perfectly
match the tacky decor found everywhere in
this condo.  As ugly as they are, they at least
do a good job of keeping the room lit.
[title25][sentence]\nYou gather from the objects over the door that\nBruce aspired to be a director.

[title29][sentence]

outfits at various theatrical events hanging
all over the walls.  Obviously, Bruce just
couldn't get enough of himself.
